definition: anxious or worried that something unpleasant may happen
example: Mia felt apprehensive before speaking in front of the class.

definition: greatly surprised or amazed
example: The audience was astonished when the quiet student won the contest.

definition: very confused and unsure what to do
example: He looked bewildered when everyone began singing.

definition: showing care and concern for someone who is suffering
chineseDefinition: 有同情心的；体恤他人的
example: The compassionate neighbour brought food to the family.

definition: showing that you think someone or something is unworthy of respect
example: She gave a contemptuous laugh at the unfair suggestion.

definition: eager to learn or know about something
example: The curious child asked how the old clock worked.

definition: having made a firm decision and not willing to give up
example: Despite the difficult climb, the team was determined to reach the summit.

definition: upset and disappointed by something unexpected
example: We were dismayed to discover that the picnic had been cancelled.

definition: extremely happy and excited
chineseDefinition: 兴高采烈的；欢欣鼓舞的
example: The players were elated after winning the final match.

definition: wanting something that another person has
example: He felt envious of his sister's new bicycle.

definition: slow to act or speak because of uncertainty
example: After a moment's pause, the hesitant swimmer stepped into the pool.

definition: angry because something seems unfair or wrong
example: The children were indignant when they were blamed for a mistake they had not made.

definition: feeling happy because worry or difficulty has ended
example: She felt relieved when her lost library book was found.

definition: unwilling or hesitant to do something
example: Although reluctant at first, Noah agreed to join the group.

definition: feeling bitter because you believe you have been treated unfairly
example: He grew resentful when his hard work went unnoticed.

definition: having doubts about whether something is true
example: The skeptical reporter asked for evidence to support the claim.

definition: suddenly surprised or frightened
example: A loud crash startled the birds in the garden.

definition: showing that you understand and care about someone's feelings
chineseDefinition: 有同情心的；表示理解的
example: Her sympathetic friend listened patiently to the whole story.

definition: very pleased because you have succeeded
example: The triumphant team waved to the crowd.

definition: careful because you do not fully trust someone or something
example: The wary fox waited until the path was quiet before crossing.

definition: expecting good things to happen
example: The coach remained optimistic about the team's chances.

definition: expecting that bad things will happen
example: Even after the setback, she refused to become pessimistic.

definition: showing that you think someone or something is unimportant
example: His dismissive reply made the others feel ignored.

definition: able to convince someone to agree or do something
chineseDefinition: 有说服力的；能劝服人的
example: Her persuasive argument encouraged the class to recycle.

definition: openly refusing to obey or accept something
example: The defiant child crossed his arms and refused to apologise.

definition: to say the opposite of what someone else has said
example: The second witness seemed to contradict the first account.

definition: to reach a conclusion using clues and evidence
example: From the muddy footprints, we can infer that someone came inside.

definition: to suggest something without stating it directly
example: The dark clouds imply that rain may be on the way.

definition: a result or effect of an action or event
example: One consequence of the storm was a fallen tree.

definition: to hide something or keep it secret
example: The squirrel tried to conceal its food beneath the leaves.

definition: not easy to find or available only in small amounts
example: During the dry season, water became scarce.

definition: easily broken or damaged
example: The fragile shell had to be carried carefully.

definition: to come out or become visible
example: The moon began to emerge from behind the clouds.

definition: to change something greatly in form or appearance
example: A little paint can transform an old room.

definition: very clear, bright, or detailed
example: The author used vivid descriptions of the rainforest.

definition: careful to avoid danger or mistakes
example: The cautious hiker checked the map before continuing.
